entities.name: PMID:26643925
observations: Prospective paired study of 20 extremely preterm infants during the first week of life; RBC transfusion increased splanchnic THI by 32.3% and sTOI by 14.6%, decreased sFTOE by 22.1%, while SMA peak systolic and diastolic velocities did not change significantly.
Supports increased intestinal tissue oxygenation without altered measured resting SMA flow velocity.

entities.name: PMID:27509230
observations: Prospective paired study of 59 preterm infants across three postnatal-age groups; RBC transfusion increased splanchnic THI and sTOI and decreased sFTOE in all groups, while SMA flow velocity did not change significantly.
Supports improved intestinal tissue oxygenation without altered measured mesenteric flow velocity across postnatal ages.

entities.name: PMID:32108891
observations: Prospective cohort of 25 stable infants born before 32 weeks and weighing under 1500 g; after 15 mL/kg PRBC transfusion, celiac flow decreased and postprandial SMA-flow augmentation failed, while first post-transfusion postprandial splanchnic FTOE increased from 10.55% to 13.21%.
Shows that transfusion-related intestinal hemodynamics are not uniformly unchanged when postprandial responses are measured.

entities.name: Transfusion oxygenation flow
observations: In two paired preterm-infant studies, RBC transfusion improved NIRS-derived splanchnic oxygenation while resting SMA Doppler velocities remained unchanged.
A separate cohort found reduced celiac flow and impaired postprandial SMA-flow augmentation, limiting universal generalization.
